title: India Eyes Six Medal Events on Action-Packed Day 2 at Glasgow Commonwealth Games
excerpt: Para powerlifting, boxing, swimming and gymnastics headline India's busiest day at CWG 2026, with competitions running from afternoon to past midnight.
body:
• India competes across six medal events on Day 2 at CWG 2026 in Glasgow, spanning para powerlifting, swimming, gymnastics, lawn bowls and boxing.
  • Para powerlifters Parmjeet Kumar, Ashok Kumar, Suman Devi and Jaspreet Kaur are among the strongest medal contenders on Friday.
  • Olympian Srihari Nataraj opens his campaign in the 50m backstroke heats, while boxer Jadumani Singh Mandengbam faces Scotland in the 55 kg Round of 32.
  • Lovlina Borgohain has already guaranteed India its first medal of the Games after receiving a bye into the boxing semi-finals.

After a glittering opening ceremony on Thursday night, India's 126-member contingent faces its busiest day of competition at the Commonwealth Games 2026 in Glasgow on Friday, with athletes scheduled across six medal events from 2:30 p.m. to past midnight, according to the Sporting News.

Para Powerlifting Leads Medal Charge

India's strongest medal prospects on Day 2 rest with the para powerlifting squad. Ashok Kumar and Parmjeet Kumar headline the Men's Lightweight Group A competition starting at 5:40 p.m., while Jaspreet Kaur and Suman Devi feature in the Women's Lightweight Group B category at 7:25 p.m., according to Revsportz. Later in the evening, Kasthuri Rajamani competes in the Women's Heavyweight event at 10:40 p.m., with Jhandu Kumar and Sudhir closing India's Day 2 schedule in the Men's Heavyweight event at 12:25 a.m.

Swimming, Gymnastics and Lawn Bowls Begin

The day's action kicks off with the men's artistic gymnastics team — Tapan Mohanty, Swatish KP, Tapeshwarnath Das and Yogeshwar Singh — beginning their team final and individual qualification at 2:30 p.m. In the pool, Olympian Srihari Nataraj starts his campaign in the Men's 50m Backstroke heats at 3:56 p.m., with a potential semi-final at 12:29 a.m. if he qualifies. Para swimmers Ravi Veera Venkata Budigina and Ali Imam contest the Men's S13 100m Freestyle heats at 3:40 p.m., with the final scheduled for midnight.

India's lawn bowls contingent continues its sectional round, with Pinki Singh and Rupa Rani Tirkey facing South Africa in the Women's Pairs at 7:30 p.m. and Putul Sonowal taking on the Falkland Islands in the Men's Singles at 10:20 p.m.

Boxing Campaign Begins

India's boxing squad opens its campaign when Jadumani Singh Mandengbam enters the ring against Scotland in the Men's 55 kg Round of 32 at 11:00 p.m. A victory would move him one step closer to the medal rounds and set the tone for a strong Indian boxing contingent that includes Olympic medallist Lovlina Borgohain, who has already guaranteed India its first medal after receiving a bye into the semi-finals, according to the Sports Tak.

Scaled-Down Games, Big Ambitions

This edition of the Commonwealth Games was scaled down after the original hosts, the state of Victoria in Australia, pulled out and Glasgow stepped in at short notice. Only 10 core sports are being held across seven venues, meaning some of India's traditionally strong disciplines — shooting, wrestling, badminton and table tennis — have missed the cut. Olympic champions Neeraj Chopra and Mirabai Chanu, along with Lovlina Borgohain, lead India's medal hopes across the 11-day competition running until August 2.

What It Means for the Diaspora

For Indian fans in the UK, Glasgow's proximity offers a rare chance to watch Indian athletes compete in person. Most afternoon sessions in Glasgow will be broadcast during the evening in India, while late-night finals may extend past midnight IST. Ahmedabad has already been confirmed as the host of the 2030 Commonwealth Games, marking India's second staging of the event after Delhi 2010.
